stations.name: Nihonbashi
stations.title: Nihon Bridge: Morning Scene
stations.note: A daimyo procession sets off across Nihonbashi at dawn as fish vendors and porters crowd the bridgehead, marking the start of the Tōkaidō in Edo.

stations.name: Shinagawa
stations.title: Shinagawa: Sunrise
stations.note: A daimyo's retinue departs from the inns of Shinagawa at sunrise, with the bay and moored boats visible beyond the rooftops.

stations.name: Kawasaki
stations.title: Kawasaki: The Rokugo Ferry
stations.note: Travelers and horses wait to board flat-bottomed ferries crossing the Tama River (Rokugo) at Kawasaki, with Mount Fuji faint in the distance.

stations.name: Kanagawa
stations.title: Kanagawa: View of the Embankment
stations.note: Teahouse touts pull at passing travelers along a steep embankment lined with waterside inns overlooking Kanagawa Bay.

stations.name: Hodogaya
stations.title: Hodogaya: Shinmachi Bridge
stations.note: A pack-horse train crosses the Shinmachi Bridge outside Hodogaya beneath windswept pines.

stations.name: Totsuka
stations.title: Totsuka: The Fork at Motomachi
stations.note: A traveler dismounts at a horse-changing station where the road forks at Motomachi, near Totsuka.

stations.name: Fujisawa
stations.title: Fujisawa: Yugyo Temple
stations.note: Pilgrims and travelers cross a bridge into Fujisawa beneath the gate of Yugyōji, the town's namesake temple, seen on the hill above.

stations.name: Hiratsuka
stations.title: Hiratsuka: Nawate Road
stations.note: Two travelers hurry along the straight embankment road (nawate) into Hiratsuka with Mount Ōyama rising behind them.

stations.name: Oiso
stations.title: Oiso: Tora's Rain
stations.note: Travelers are caught in a sudden shower on the shore road at Ōiso, a rain traditionally called "Tora ga ame" after the legendary courtesan Tora.

stations.name: Odawara
stations.title: Odawara: The Sakawa River
stations.note: Porters carry a palanquin and baggage across the shallow Sakawa River on the approach to Odawara Castle, visible on the far bank.

stations.name: Hakone
stations.title: Hakone: View of the Lake
stations.note: A daimyo procession winds along a jagged mountain trail above Lake Ashi, with the peaks of the Hakone range towering over the water.

stations.name: Mishima
stations.title: Mishima: Morning Mist
stations.note: Travelers and a packhorse emerge from thick morning fog near the torii gate of Mishima Taisha, Mount Fuji hidden entirely from view.

stations.name: Numazu
stations.title: Numazu: Twilight
stations.note: A pilgrim in a tengu mask and a pack-laden traveler walk along the Kano River at dusk beneath a full moon, geese overhead.

stations.name: Hara
stations.title: Hara: Mount Fuji in the Morning
stations.note: Two travelers cross a marshy plain at Hara beneath an enormous Mount Fuji filling the sky.

stations.name: Yoshiwara
stations.title: Yoshiwara: Mount Fuji on the Left
stations.note: Riders and porters follow a bend in the road at Yoshiwara from which Mount Fuji unusually appears on the left side of the frame.

stations.name: Kanbara
stations.title: Kanbara: Evening Snow
stations.note: Three muffled figures trudge through a silent, heavy snowfall in Kanbara, a scene of snow the town rarely saw.

stations.name: Yui
stations.title: Yui: Satta Peak
stations.note: Travelers pause on the cliffside Satta Pass trail overlooking Suruga Bay, with Mount Fuji visible across the water.

stations.name: Okitsu
stations.title: Okitsu: The Okitsu River
stations.note: Porters ford the shallow Okitsu River carrying a mounted traveler and baggage toward the town.

stations.name: Ejiri
stations.title: Ejiri: Distant View of Miho
stations.note: Boats sail Suruga Bay off Ejiri as the pine-covered spit of Miho stretches into the distance beneath Mount Fuji.

stations.name: Fuchū
stations.title: Fuchū: The Abe River
stations.note: Porters carry passengers and palanquins on their shoulders across the wide, shallow Abe River outside Fuchū.

stations.name: Mariko
stations.title: Mariko: Famous Tea Shop
stations.note: Travelers stop at a thatched roadside teahouse in Mariko famous for its grated-yam (tororo) soup, served by a woman with a child.

stations.name: Okabe
stations.title: Okabe: Utsu Mountain
stations.note: A line of travelers threads a narrow, tree-shaded mountain path over the Utsu Pass near Okabe.

stations.name: Fujieda
stations.title: Fujieda: Changing Porters and Horses
stations.note: Porters and packhorses are exchanged at the station entrance to Fujieda as a new relay team takes over the baggage.

stations.name: Shimada
stations.title: Shimada: The Suruga Bank of the Oi River
stations.note: Porters and mounted travelers gather on the Suruga-side bank of the Ōi River at Shimada, waiting to be carried across since no bridge was permitted.

stations.name: Kanaya
stations.title: Kanaya: The Far Bank of the Oi River
stations.note: Palanquin bearers wade the Ōi River toward Kanaya on the river's far bank, mountains rising beyond.

stations.name: Nissaka
stations.title: Nissaka: Sayo Mountain Pass
stations.note: A traveler rests beside a huge roadside boulder on the steep Sayo-no-Nakayama pass above Nissaka.

stations.name: Kakegawa
stations.title: Kakegawa: Distant View of Mount Akiba
stations.note: A kite flies over a river crossing near Kakegawa with the sacred peak of Mount Akiba visible on the horizon.

stations.name: Fukuroi
stations.title: Fukuroi: Tea Stall
stations.note: Travelers rest at an open-air tea stall on the plain outside Fukuroi, one of the smaller stations on the route.

stations.name: Mitsuke
stations.title: Mitsuke: View of the Tenryu River
stations.note: Ferrymen pole passengers across the broad Tenryū River near Mitsuke, with sandbars and distant hills beyond.

stations.name: Hamamatsu
stations.title: Hamamatsu: Winter Scene
stations.note: Travelers warm themselves at a bonfire beneath a huge bare tree on the outskirts of Hamamatsu, Mount Fuji faint in the distance.

stations.name: Maisaka
stations.title: Maisaka: View of Imagiri
stations.note: Sailboats cross the calm waters of Lake Hamana at the Imagiri crossing near Maisaka, with Mount Fuji on the horizon.

stations.name: Arai
stations.title: Arai: View of Ferryboats
stations.note: A daimyo's ferry approaches the shore at the Arai checkpoint, one of the Tōkaidō's most heavily guarded barrier stations.

stations.name: Shirasuka
stations.title: Shirasuka: View of Shiomi Slope
stations.note: Travelers pause on the Shiomizaka hillside above Shirasuka, where the road briefly opens onto a view of the sea.

stations.name: Futagawa
stations.title: Futagawa: Sarugababa Plateau
stations.note: A modest teahouse stands alone on the windswept Sarugababa plateau outside Futagawa as a samurai procession passes.

stations.name: Yoshida
stations.title: Yoshida: The Toyo River Bridge
stations.note: Workers repair the long wooden bridge over the Toyo River at Yoshida beneath the walls of Yoshida Castle.

stations.name: Goyu
stations.title: Goyu: Women Stopping Travelers
stations.note: Innkeepers' women physically pull passing travelers by the sleeve into competing lodging houses at Goyu.

stations.name: Akasaka
stations.title: Akasaka: Waitresses at an Inn
stations.note: Serving women prepare an evening meal and entertain guests in the courtyard of an inn at Akasaka.

stations.name: Fujikawa
stations.title: Fujikawa: View of Post Outskirts
stations.note: A small daimyo procession passes a solitary teahouse at the edge of Fujikawa as evening approaches.

stations.name: Okazaki
stations.title: Okazaki: Yahagi Bridge
stations.note: A daimyo procession crosses the immense Yahagi Bridge into Okazaki beneath its castle, one of the longest bridges on the Tōkaidō.

stations.name: Chiryū
stations.title: Chiryū: Early Summer Horse Market
stations.note: Horses are bought and sold in an open field outside Chiryū during the town's famous early-summer horse market.

stations.name: Narumi
stations.title: Narumi: Famous Tie-dyed Fabrics of Arimatsu
stations.note: Shops in Narumi display bolts of the tie-dyed cotton (Arimatsu shibori) for which the town was famous, as travelers browse.

stations.name: Miya
stations.title: Miya: Religious Festival at Atsuta Shrine
stations.note: Wrestlers perform sumo before a crowd during a festival at Atsuta Shrine, the landmark of the port town of Miya.

stations.name: Kuwana
stations.title: Kuwana: The Landing of the Shichiri Ferry Crossing
stations.note: Sailboats approach the pier at Kuwana after the seven-ri sea crossing from Miya, since no direct road linked the two towns.

stations.name: Yokkaichi
stations.title: Yokkaichi: Mie River
stations.note: A traveler's straw hat blows away in the wind as he crosses a plank bridge over the Mie River outside Yokkaichi.

stations.name: Ishiyakushi
stations.title: Ishiyakushi: Ishiyakushi Temple
stations.note: A quiet view of Ishiyakushi Temple and its surrounding pines is seen from the road, with little traffic on this small station.

stations.name: Shōno
stations.title: Shōno: Driving Rain
stations.note: Travelers and porters are caught in a sudden, driving rainstorm as they hurry along the road at Shōno.

stations.name: Kameyama
stations.title: Kameyama: Weather Clearing after Snow
stations.note: A procession climbs a steep, snow-covered slope toward Kameyama Castle as the sky clears after a snowfall.

stations.name: Seki
stations.title: Seki: Early Departure from the Main Camp
stations.note: Porters and a palanquin assemble in the pre-dawn dark outside the honjin (main inn) at Seki as a party prepares to depart.

stations.name: Sakanoshita
stations.title: Sakanoshita: Peak of Fudesute Mountain
stations.note: Travelers pause at a teahouse overlooking a dramatic gorge and waterfall near the peak of Fudesute-yama.

stations.name: Tsuchiyama
stations.title: Tsuchiyama: Spring Shower
stations.note: Travelers cross a bridge over a swollen mountain stream at Tsuchiyama in a sudden spring downpour.

stations.name: Minakuchi
stations.title: Minakuchi: Dried Gourd Shavings, A Local Specialty
stations.note: Women prepare and dry kanpyō (gourd shavings), the local specialty of Minakuchi, on racks outside a farmhouse.

stations.name: Ishibe
stations.title: Ishibe: Megawa Village
stations.note: Travelers pass through the small hamlet of Megawa near Ishibe as the sun rises over distant hills.

stations.name: Kusatsu
stations.title: Kusatsu: Famous Post House
stations.note: Palanquin bearers and travelers crowd a large post-house courtyard at Kusatsu, where the Tōkaidō met the Nakasendō.

stations.name: Ōtsu
stations.title: Ōtsu: Hashirii Teahouse
stations.note: Ox-carts loaded with goods pass a well-known teahouse at the edge of Ōtsu on the final approach to Kyoto.

stations.name: Kyoto
stations.title: Kyoto: The Great Bridge at Sanjo
stations.note: Travelers and ox-carts cross the Sanjō Ōhashi bridge into Kyoto, with the city and hills beyond marking the end of the Tōkaidō.
